reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT still matches Y{1,4}, and Y/YYY tokens not implemented in format() fall through to the zoneStr fallback, formatting as a timezone offset (e.g. +0000) instead of the literal 'Y' / '24Y' the test expects.

The regex now matches only YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' stays a literal character and 'YYY' becomes the two-digit year plus literal 'Y' ('24Y'), exactly what the test expects; the offset fallback no longer applies to these tokens.
The percent-decoding logic already existed at base and correctly decoded %20 to a space; the PR only extracts the same check into a shared tryDecodeURIComponent utility, preserving behavior.

The refactor moves the identical 'contains %' check into tryDecodeURIComponent in utils/url.ts and calls it from the same code paths, so percent-encoded params are still decoded to their original characters.
At base, reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so reading entry.score/entry.at off the same in-memory handle returns the stale pre-reschedule time.
The fix adds @score = at.to_f after zincrby, so the in-memory SortedEntry immediately reports the newly requested reschedule time from the same handle.
The PR only changes parseRangesSpecifier in Ranges.kt (Range header whitespace handling); Content-Type parsing with charset parameters is untouched and behaves as expected at base.
Only Range header parsing is modified; Content-Type/charset parsing is in unrelated code and still reports 'text/plain' with charset 'UTF-8'.
The PR only alters log/error messages in ComposerRepository.php; zip archive creation is handled elsewhere and still preserves source file timestamps at base.
The change is confined to download-failure logging in ComposerRepository; archiving logic is untouched, so re-archiving still yields source-matching timestamps with no 1980 dates.

The PR modifies CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix in System.Net; JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync is unaffected, so asynchronous deserialization of the nullable-parent structure succeeds without JsonException at base.
Only CredentialCache prefix matching is changed; sync and async JSON deserialization both keep working and produce equivalent object graphs.
The PR touches only cursor FETCH FIRST logic in sql_cursor.go; INET operators like <<= ANY are unaffected and the query parses and returns true at base.
The change is limited to fetchMoveNodeBase cursor handling; INET >>= ANY semantics are untouched, so the statement executes and returns true without syntax errors.

At base, every NO_PROXY entry is prefixed with a wildcard (all://*::1); the PR description states such an IPv6 entry becomes a pattern the URL parsing step cannot interpret, so client construction raises.
The fix detects '::1' via is_ipv6_hostname and registers all://[::1] as a bypass mount, so client construction succeeds and normal requests still work.
At base, flags other than IGNORECASE (like DOTALL) fail the strict compiled-pattern flag equality check, so the match call with the newline-matching option is rejected with an error.
The fix restores support for non-IGNORECASE flags: DOTALL is preserved through compilation and comparison, so 'a.c' matches 'a\nc' and not 'ac' for both forms of the request.
At base, freezing a chain containing a group in the middle loses the group's child results (the bug this PR fixes), so the reconstructed result tree lacks the four group children.
The prepare_steps fix keeps prev_task/prev_res pointed at the group, so the frozen/serialized chain retains a separate child result for every task in both parallel groups.

At base, the hyphen-handling path treats '--' as entering trailing-values mode without consulting the current positional's value_terminator, causing the first positional to capture everything after the '--' instead of handing off to the second positional.

The fix makes the positional's value_terminator take precedence over trailing-values mode when it matches '--', so the first positional stops at value2 and the second collects '--check' without parse errors.
At base the OSC11 handler calls nvim_set_option_value('background', ...) directly, which fires OptionSet (and ColorScheme) when the response arrives after startup, matching the expected result.
The fix wraps the background assignment in :noautocmd, deliberately suppressing the OptionSet event; the test expects both OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands to fire, so OptionSet no longer does.

The PR only reorders when the @derive attribute is read at schema compile time; changeset casting and validate_required are untouched, so an omitted required field still marks the changeset invalid at base.
The compile-time @derive read reordering has no runtime effect on changesets; required-field validation still flags the omitted field with a 'can't be blank' error.
